questions.title: Question 1: Arrays.sort, strings and the array-to-list code (10 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) State what `Arrays.sort` and `Arrays.toString` do and the time complexity of sorting. (b) Give the output of `Integer[] arr = {73, 64, 59, 15, 91, 27, 82}; Arrays.sort(arr); System.out.println("Integer Array is: " + Arrays.toString(arr));`. (c) State the order of the `String` array `{"pear", "Apple", "banana", "apple"}` after `Arrays.sort`, and why. (d) The lecture's `(Arrays.asList(marks));` and `aList.toArray(marks)` do not compile: give the two compiler messages and the repair. (10 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: `Arrays.sort` sorts the array in ascending order by default, with no loop to write: primitives use an adaptation of quick sort, objects an adaptation of merge sort (Timsort), in time `O(n log n)`. `Arrays.toString` returns the `String` representation of the array. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: `[Apple, apple, banana, pear]`. Strings are ordered by the Unicode values of their characters, so uppercase `A` (65) comes before lowercase `a` (97), and `apple` is before `banana` because `a` is before `b`. (2 marks)

steps.title: Part (d)
steps.body: `(Arrays.asList(marks));` gives `error: not a statement`; `aList` gives `error: cannot find symbol` (variable aList). Repair: `ArrayList<Integer> myList = new ArrayList<Integer>(Arrays.asList(marks)); myList.add(70); marks = myList.toArray(marks);`. The result of `toArray` is assigned because the 4-cell array is too small for 5 elements, so a new array is returned. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** `[15, 27, 59, 64, 73, 82, 91]` and `[Apple, apple, banana, pear]`; the repaired code ends with `Marks : [73, 81, 69, 60, 70]`.

questions.title: Question 2: An iterator that removes (10 marks)
questions.prompt: A list holds `[51, 35, 12, 81, 54, 16]` and `it = list.iterator()`. (a) Give the value returned by each of `it.next(); it.next(); it.next();`, then the list after `it.remove();`, then the value of the next `it.next()`. (b) Say what is thrown by `remove()` before any `next()`, by `next()` past the end, and by `list.remove(...)` inside a for-each loop over `[73, 92, 58, 60]` when the 92 is removed. (c) Write a loop with an iterator that removes every even number. (10 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: The three calls return 51, 35 and 12. `remove()` removes the last element seen, 12, so the list is `[51, 35, 81, 54, 16]`, and the next `it.next()` returns 81. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `remove()` before any `next()`: `IllegalStateException`. `next()` with no next element: `NoSuchElementException`. Removing 92 inside a for-each loop: `ConcurrentModificationException` (the for-each uses an iterator privately). (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: `Iterator<Integer> it = list.iterator(); while (it.hasNext()) { if (it.next() % 2 == 0) { it.remove(); } }`. One `next()` is made per `hasNext()`. For `[73, 92, 58, 60]` the result is `[73]`. (3 marks)

questions.title: Question 3: List operations and their errors (12 marks)
questions.prompt: Start with `List<Integer> marks = new ArrayList<Integer>();`. Give the list after each of `add(84)`, `add(62)`, `add(2, 73)` and `add(73)`, and its size. Then explain why `add(9, 1)` and `remove(84)` throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException`, and how to remove the value 84. (12 marks)

steps.title: The operations
steps.body: `[84]`, `[84, 62]`, then `add(2, 73)` gives `[84, 62, 73]` because index 2 equals `size()`, which is the position just after the last element (the lecture slide marks it as an error, but with two elements it runs), then `add(73)` gives `[84, 62, 73, 73]`. The size is 4 and `isEmpty()` is `false`. (5 marks)

steps.title: The exceptions
steps.body: `add(9, 1)`: the valid indexes for `add(i, e)` are 0 to `size()`, here 0 to 4, so 9 throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. `remove(84)`: 84 is an `int`, so `remove(int index)` is chosen and there is no index 84. (4 marks)

steps.title: Removing the value
steps.body: `marks.remove(Integer.valueOf(84))` calls `remove(Object)` and removes the first element equal to 84, giving `[62, 73, 73]`. (3 marks)

questions.title: Question 4: A Comparable Book (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) Write class `Book` with `title` and `year` that implements `Comparable<Book>` so that books are ordered by year. (b) Show the output of sorting `("Java Programming", 2003)`, `("Learn Java", 2014)` and `("Java is Fun", 2000)` with `Collections.sort`. (c) Explain what goes wrong if `compareTo` compares only the year but `equals` compares title and year. (d) State what happens when `Collections.sort` is called on a list of a class that is not `Comparable`. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: `class Book implements Comparable<Book>`, with `public int compareTo(Book bk) { if (year == bk.year) return 0; else if (year > bk.year) return 1; else return -1; }`. It must cater for the negative, positive and zero cases. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `Java is Fun 2000`, `Java Programming 2003`, `Learn Java 2014`: ascending order of year. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: Two books with the same year and different titles give `compareTo == 0` but `equals` false, so the ordering is not consistent with `equals`. Repair: when the years are equal, return `title.compareTo(other.title)`. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (d)
steps.body: `Collections.sort(list)` does not compile: `no suitable method found for sort(List<...>)`. `Arrays.sort` on an array of such objects compiles and throws `ClassCastException` at run time. (2 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** The books print in the order 2000, 2003, 2014.

questions.title: Question 5: The Person tester (14 marks)
questions.prompt: Describe the Lab 8 question 1 program: the class `Person`, how the tester reads six records from a file into an `ArrayList`, what happens at `remove(2)` and `remove(8)`, and the order after `Collections.sort`. The records are `265341,Lesego Jones,19`, `265476,Thomas Kago,25`, `673523,Mpho Wangu,28`, `118204,Neo Dube,22`, `540912,Kagiso Moeng,31` and `722301,Amo Seretse,20`. (14 marks)

steps.title: The class
steps.body: `Person` has `id`, `fullname` and `age`, implements `Comparable<Person>` with `compareTo` returning `fullname.compareTo(other.fullname)`, and overrides `toString` and `equals` (with `instanceof` and a cast). (4 marks)

steps.title: Reading and removing
steps.body: The file is read one line at a time: `split(",")`, `Integer.parseInt` for the id and the age, and each `Person` is added to the list (six items). `remove(2)` removes Mpho Wangu and shifts the later items left (five items). `remove(8)` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` because the valid indexes are 0 to 4; the list does not change. (6 marks)

steps.title: Sorting
steps.body: `Collections.sort` orders by `compareTo`, that is, by `fullname`: Amo Seretse, Kagiso Moeng, Lesego Jones, Neo Dube, Thomas Kago. (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Five items remain after `remove(2)`; `remove(8)` throws; the sorted order starts with Amo Seretse.

questions.title: Question 6: The course LinkedList (12 marks)
questions.prompt: A `LinkedList<String>` gets `add("Data Structures")`, `add("Probability")`, `addLast("Networks")`, `add("Operating Systems")` and `addFirst("Databases")`, then `removeFirst()` and `removeLast()`, then `add("Programming")`, `add("Calculus")` and `add(5, "Statistics")`. Give the list after the first five statements, after the two removals and at the end, then its sorted order and say why the `add(5, ...)` call is valid. (12 marks)

steps.title: After the adds
steps.body: `[Databases, Data Structures, Probability, Networks, Operating Systems]`. (3 marks)

steps.title: After the removals
steps.body: `removeFirst()` returns Databases and `removeLast()` returns Operating Systems, leaving `[Data Structures, Probability, Networks]`. (3 marks)

steps.title: The end
steps.body: After `Programming` and `Calculus` the list has five elements, so index 5 equals `size()` and `add(5, "Statistics")` adds at the end: `[Data Structures, Probability, Networks, Programming, Calculus, Statistics]`. With only three elements it would throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. (3 marks)

steps.title: Sorted
steps.body: `Collections.sort` gives `[Calculus, Data Structures, Networks, Probability, Programming, Statistics]`. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Six courses at the end; the sorted list starts with Calculus.
